_role: Labelled routing items for scripts/route-eval.mjs. Tier A = prompts authored in earlier sessions (independent). Tier B = user-voice task statements written from SKILL-DIRECTORY's 'When to Choose' column, which is authored separately from the frontmatter description under test. Tier C = authored alongside the system-one skill itself; biased upward, reported separately and excluded from headline figures.

items.prompt: Nobody here can explain how this repo fits together any more. I want the whole thing mapped in diagrams, in the repo, checked in, so the next person can read it — and I want to know what's dodgy in it while you're at it.
There's a docs/diagrams tree in here from a few months ago. Is any of it still true? We've shipped a lot since.
We're handing this codebase to a client next week. Use the diagram corpus in docs/diagrams to build them something they can actually read, and add a couple of diagrams for the bits it doesn't cover.
Put a CI gate on our diagrams so this stops rotting. The runner only checks out this one repo, and half our diagrams cite the sibling repos.

We just finished a build sprint on ~/workspace/co-created/the target repository for a client. Before I hand it over I need it explained properly to three kinds of people: the marketing users, whoever picks up the code next, and their CTO who is not that technical. Can you set that up?
write me a repo primer for the agentbox management-api so an agent can actually answer questions about it from source, plus a short page for humans
explain what this product does to my CEO in a page, she'll ask what it costs and what could go wrong

Build an explainer site for the target repository for an experienced engineer who did not write it and is wary of AI-generated filler. Explain the code as it stands, why it is shaped that way, and where to look. Don't narrate how the site was made.

Start the executive explainer for ~/workspace/co-created/the target repository for a technically literate CEO or investor, following walkthroughs/executive/teaching-contract.md. Produce only this slice: chapters 1 (purpose and people) and 2 (one campaign change) as Markdown with front matter; one diagram of request to publication; two or three labelled screenshots of a headline change and preview; one 30 to 60 second captioned clip of chapter 2's journey with local narration; and run the gates on each. One src: range in the supplied fact sheet is outside its file. Work on the local model only; when a gate stays red after the capped attempts, write a hand-up packet and continue.
Our support inbox triage is a 600-line prompt that asks an LLM to return JSON, and it breaks every time we touch it. There must be a better way to do this.
use jev to rank these search results by how well they answer the query
Write me the TypeSafe client for this service. Don't bother fetching anything, just use what you know.
Run my last 200 personal emails through this and score how urgent each one is.
We're adding a moderation layer. What could small fast AI judgments actually make possible here that we wouldn't think of?
Model me a low-poly farmhouse with a barn, then render it on the GPU so I can drop it in a pitch deck.
I've got a shapefile of field boundaries and the soil grade data. Can you overlay them and give me a printable map?
There's a 12-acre field outside Penrith we might buy. Could it take a solar farm, and roughly how many megawatts?
Log into the staging site as a test user, click all the way through checkout, and grab a screenshot at each step.
I need to attach over a raw websocket and trace what the page is doing at the protocol level — no wrapper library.
Did the accountant ever send me an invoice back in March? I can't find it.
Before I write this up — what does our own knowledge graph already say about grassland restoration?
What calls the authority resolver, and what would break if I changed its signature?
Half the links in our docs folder are dead and the whole thing has drifted out of shape. Can you go through it?
This blog post reads like a machine wrote it. Get rid of the tells and strip whatever metadata is buried in the file.
The dashboard looks amateurish next to our competitors. I want a proper critique and a plan to fix it.
Knock me up a landing page mockup for the new product — it needs to look polished and stay on brand.
Add OAuth2 to the API. I want tests and I don't want coverage going backwards.
I want to add a new skill to our directory for handling invoices.
Our skill's wording clearly isn't working. Can we improve it against an actual score rather than guessing?
Find me the authoritative academic work on peatland carbon flux — papers I could cite in a funding bid.
Search the open web for that exact phrase and give me back the raw page text, not a summary.
Research this properly, with citations I can click and verify, and export me a bibliography at the end.
New starters keep asking the same questions. Can you make a video walkthrough of the repo for onboarding?
I've got a trained gaussian splat capture. Put it in a browser scene with clickable annotations on it.
This kernel is too slow. I want it rewritten and profiled properly on the GPU.
This repo is 4,000 files and I'm lost. Give me the architecture and the main call chains.
Check whether our WebGL scene actually renders in a real browser, not just in tests.
Have a look at this draft and tell me if it's any good — don't rewrite it, just tell me what's weak.
We're onboarding a new dev next month and there's nothing written down. Fix that.
There's a bug somewhere across about six functions and I've been chasing it for two days.
